stage1.impression: A strong idea: a low camera, a lone amber speaker in a rain-swept wasteland under a bright storm horizon, with a puddle channel leading the eye to it. The execution still reads as CG. The cabinet is lit flat, like matte yellow plastic, with both visible faces the same value. Its reflection is an opaque, hard-edged copy with no ripple break-up. The 'black volcanic rock' reads as soft grey clay with denoiser smear. The rain is too sparse to read as a storm against the ground.

blocking_9: The cabinet's two visible faces separate in value (left face at least 15 % darker than the front), and its acrylic edges glow amber against the sky band, so it reads as cast acrylic and not painted plastic
The puddle reflection is broken by ripples and splashes, with a soft, wavering edge and no clean straight copy of the cabinet
The ground reads as wet black basalt: near-black base (lum median under 35) with sharp sky-band specular glints on the water film, and real grain in the foreground with no denoise smear
Rain is legible across the whole frame, against the dark ground as well as the sky, as backlit streaks catching the low light
The cabinet's colour stays inside gamut (the blue channel above zero on the lit faces), so the yellow has tonal gradation and is not posterized
Final at 2400 x 1600 with enough samples that no denoiser smear shows in the foreground rock or the water

defects.what: Cabinet lit flat: left face and front face both measure lum median about 91-92; it reads as matte painted plastic, not tinted acrylic
Cabinet blue channel at 0 on the lit faces (r129 g91 b0): saturation is clipped and gradation is posterized
Reflection is a near-perfect straight copy with hard vertical edges (10-90 width 15 px at x 680-720) and almost no ripple distortion; lum_range only 50
Ground reads as grey-olive clay or mud (median 43, g44 b32), not wet black basalt; blobby displacement; no specular glints from the water film
Foreground puddle and rock edges are mushy, with denoiser smear and no micro-detail at the frame's sharpest-looking distance
Puddle bank on the right reads as soft modelled clay with a slick, uniform edge; the water's shoreline is too smooth and too even
Rain streaks are nearly invisible against the ground; the storm reads only in the sky
Left ridge lit bright green (lum median 184) reads as a small pasted hill, brighter than the far field around it
Waterline at the cabinet base: no meniscus, no ripple ring and no splash at the contact; it looks set onto the surface
Horn's reflections are busy (lum_range 220) with an orange hot specular that pulls the eye above the cabinet

changes.problem: The cabinet is lit flat: the 2 m reflector at 40 deg left fills the left face to the same value as the front, so the form vanishes and the acrylic reads as plastic.

evidence.measured: left face lum_median 92.3 vs front face top band [560,380,690,410] lum_median 90.9; no separation between the planes

change.to: move to 70 deg left, irradiance 1.2; raise the right rim card from 2.0 to 3.0 so the right edge and the acrylic edges catch the low light

changes.expected: The left face falls about half a stop below the front; the right edge glows amber against the bright band; the cabinet gains volume.

changes.problem: The puddle mirrors the cabinet as a hard, straight copy, which is the frame's strongest 'render' tell in a scene with drops hitting the water.

evidence.measured: reflection lum_range 50.3, falloff flat (bins 45-55); right edge 10-90 width 15 px

change.setting: Puddles: surface roughness and ripple rings
change.from: roughness 0.01, largest rings at half strength, 450 splashes at opacity 0.12
change.to: roughness 0.02, all ring layers at full strength, add a fine wind ripple (2-4 cm wavelength, low amplitude) across the chain, splashes 1200 at opacity 0.25 concentrated within 3 m of the speaker

changes.expected: The reflection breaks into wavering bands with bright ring highlights; it still reads as the speaker, but as water and not a mirror.

changes.problem: The ground reads as grey-olive clay, not wet black volcanic rock: too light, too green, and the water film shows no glints.

change.to: darkened 75 %, tinted #121210 at 85 %, clear coat 0.8 with roughness 0.02 to 0.08, so the sky band streaks across the wet tops

changes.expected: A near-black base with sharp cream glints on the ridges of the rock. The amber speaker becomes the only warm, saturated thing in the frame.

changes.problem: The cabinet's yellow is clipped out of gamut, with the blue channel at 0, so the colour posterizes into flat fields.

change.to: 5700 K, tint -12; get the sulphurous green from the haze colour and the sky grade, not from the global balance

changes.expected: The cabinet keeps a little blue and shows tonal gradation across its faces; the sky stays yellow-green.

changes.problem: The rain reads only against the sky; against the ground the storm disappears, so the 'acid rain, real' idea is half-told.

evidence.measured: seen: almost no streaks visible against the ground band; ground p95 66 to 81 with no thin bright verticals

change.from: 65,000 streaks, opacity 0.1 to 0.45, half as many below 1.5 m
change.to: 140,000 streaks, opacity 0.2 to 0.6, the same density below 1.5 m between 5 and 25 m, so the backlit streaks read against the dark rock; forward scattering raised so they catch the low sun

changes.expected: Thin bright streaks read across the dark ground on both sides of the speaker, densest in the mid-ground behind it.

changes.problem: The waterline at the cabinet's base has no interaction, so the speaker looks set onto the water and not standing in it.

evidence.measured: seen: clean straight junction between the cabinet and its reflection, no meniscus or rings

change.setting: Puddles and splashes at the speaker
change.to: add a ring of drip impacts and 2 to 3 ripple rings (8 to 20 cm) spreading from the cabinet's base, plus a thin meniscus highlight along the waterline

changes.expected: A broken bright line and rings at the base give the speaker weight and contact with the water.

changes.problem: The left ridge reads as a small, bright green pasted hill, and the far field under it is uniform.

evidence.measured: lum_median 184.5, rgb 188/190/122, brighter and greener than the far field (lum_median 123 at [800,435,1200,460])

change.to: darken the ridge's material 50 % and set haze to 0.0025 /m, so the ridge sits as a dim silhouette in the rain haze

changes.expected: The ridge becomes a faint grey-green silhouette slightly darker than the sky band behind it, adding depth instead of drawing the eye.

changes.problem: The foreground rock and the puddle banks are smeared by the denoiser, so the nearest surfaces have no micro-detail.

evidence.measured: seen at 3x: mushy, blotchy texture with no grain at the rock edges; lum_range 98 is mostly from broad blobs, not detail

change.to: 1024 samples at 2400 x 1600, denoiser with albedo and normal passes at reduced strength (or blend 30 % of the noisy pass back), clarity 0.07 to 0.12 on the ground only

changes.expected: Real grain and pores in the foreground basalt and crisp ripple highlights, with no fireflies.

out_of_scope.request: Calm the horn's busy internal reflections and its orange hot specular, which pull the eye above the cabinet
out_of_scope.why: The horn's resin, shape and finish are part of the speaker; only the light on it may change (c1's rim card may help).
